candidate.answerReason: The equal perpendicular distances place the interior point P on the angle bisector. Since OD lies along OA, the whole angle is twice 25°, giving 50°.

methods.label: Apply the angle bisector criterion
methods.explanation: Since \(PD=PE\) and \(P\) lies inside the angle, \(OP\) bisects \(\angle AOB\), so \(\angle AOB=2\times25^\circ=50^\circ\).
methods.levelReason: The angle bisector criterion is Grade 8 geometry, supported by perpendicular distance and elementary angle calculations.

candidate.annotationRationale:
The target is recognizing the angle bisector from equal distances to the sides. The retained method applies cnm_129 directly; cnm_065 interprets the perpendicular segments as distances, and cnm_058 supports doubling the half-angle. A separate proof of the criterion would add unnecessary detail here.
